smt-2021-nt-tiebreaker-02.title: Middle divisor pairs
smt-2021-nt-tiebreaker-02.body:
If $n$ is a perfect square the median is $\sqrt n$, an integer, which cannot lie strictly between $20$ and $21$. Otherwise the median is $\frac{d+e}2$ where $d<e$ are the two middle divisors and $de=n$, and $20<\frac{d+e}2<21$ means $d+e=41$. So $n=d(41-d)$ for some $d\le20$, with no divisor of $n$ strictly between $d$ and $41-d$. Checking $d=1,\dots,20$ leaves $n=148,310,348,390,408,414,418,420$ (for example $148$ has divisors $1,2,4,37,74,148$). Their sum is $2856$.

**Answer: 2856**

smt-2021-nt-tiebreaker-03.title: Sum of two squares
smt-2021-nt-tiebreaker-03.body:
A positive integer is a sum of two squares iff every prime $\equiv3\pmod4$ divides it to an even power. $20!=2^{18}3^85^47^2\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19$. A random divisor has independent exponents, uniform on their ranges. The primes $3,7,11,19$ are $3\bmod4$: the probability of an even exponent is $\frac59$ (for $3$: exponents $0..8$), $\frac23$ (for $7$: $0..2$), $\frac12$ (for $11$) and $\frac12$ (for $19$). Probability $=\frac59\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac5{54}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{54}$**
